name: Chey Tae-won
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Chey Tae-won is the chairman of SK Group, one of Korea's largest conglomerates with interests in telecom, semiconductors, chemicals and energy, among others.
The group's SK Telecom is South Korea's No. 1 mobile carrier by market share; its SK Hynix is the world's second-largest memory chipmaker by sales.
In 2013 he was convicted of misappropriating company funds but was later pardoned by then-president Park Geun-hye and returned to his post in 2016.
Chey is a nephew of SK Group founder Chey Jong-gun, who started the conglomerate with a textile company called Sunkyong.
forbes_facts: While in jail, he authored a book on social enterprises.
Chey filed for divorce from his wife, a daughter of former South Korean President Roh Tae-woo in 2017. In 2024, Chey was ordered to pay $1 billion to his ex-wife.

name: Airat Shaimiev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Airat Shaimiev made his fortune as a co-owner of the TAIF Group, a large regional holding company with assets in the Republic of Tatarstan.
In 2021, TAIF merged with petrochemical company Sibur. He and other TAIF shareholders got 15% of Sibur in exchange.
Shaimiev is also CEO of Tatautodor, the government-owned group that does road construction and repair in Tatarstan.
forbes_facts: Airat's father, Mintimer Shaimiev, was Tatarstan's first president; his brother, Radik is also a billionaire.
Airat, his brother Radik and Airat's son Timur together own a small oil company, MNKT, in Tatarstan.

name: Kirill Shamalov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2016-2018); Hurun Global (2017)
forbes_bio: Kirill Shamalov is the son of Rossiya Bank shareholder Nikolai Shamalov, a longtime friend of Putin.
Shamalov studied law at Saint Petersburg State University and became vice president of Russian petrochemical company Sibur at age 26.
In 2014, he bought a stake in Sibur from billionaire Gennady Timchenko, a longtime friend of Putin's who was the target of U.S. sanctions.
He later sold most of his stake but still held onto roughly 4% of Sibur.
forbes_facts: Kirill Shamalov was married to President Vladimir Putin's daughter, academic Katerina Tikhonova, according to sources.
Their marriage was dissolved sometime in 2016 or 2017, which is around when Shamalov sold a 17% stake in Sibur.

name: Caroline Cochran
forbes_bio: Cochran cofounded Oklo with her husband, Jacob DeWitte, in 2013. She is chief operating officer, while DeWitte is CEO.
Cochran and DeWitte own 16% of the company combined.
Oklo went public in 2024 at a valuation of $1 billion, after merging with a Sam Altman-backed special purpose acquisition company.
Before starting Oklo, Cochran graduated from MIT with a masters degree in nuclear engineering and worked as a marketing and engineering consultant.
Oklo's name comes from the uranium-rich mineral deposits at Oklo, Gabon, known for undergoing self-sustained fission two billion years ago.
